advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure create_defaults cannot re-inject a computed field (esp. priority/status) that map-or-drift intentionally omitted — restrict defaults to non-baseline keys or merge only keys absent from the baseline field set (not merely absent from the drift-omitted result).
evidence: outbound_mapper.py:82-84 docstring: 'The baseline computed ``result`` ALWAYS wins on collision — a default that names a field the mapper already computes (``summary``/``priority``/...) never overrides it'
outbound_fields.py:173-175 — on drift `result['priority']` is never set, so it is ABSENT from `result` when merge runs at line 243
ABSENCE: no guard rejects or filters create_defaults keys that name baseline/optional computed fields (summary/priority/status/issuetype/assignee/parent) before merging
advisory.finding: merge_create_defaults ({**create_defaults, **result}) can silently re-inject a `priority` (or `status`) value that map-or-drift deliberately OMITTED from the computed body, because on drift that key is absent from `result` so a create_defaults entry naming it is not overridden. This contradicts the merge docstring's claim that a default 'never overrides' a computed field like `priority`, and defeats the S5 guarantee that a drifting priority leaves Jira unchanged.
scenarios: A project config sets [mapping.projects.K.create_defaults] priority = "Medium" AND a ticket has an out-of-range/unmapped local priority: the create body ends up with priority="Medium" even though map-or-drift intended to omit it (regression toward the very Medium-coercion this story removed).
A create_defaults entry naming `status` re-introduces a status that drifted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Filter create_defaults to keys that are NOT in the mapper's known baseline/computed field set (summary, description, issuetype, priority, status, assignee, parent) before merging, so a default can only ever inject a truly required-beyond-baseline vendor field and can never resurrect a drifted priority/status.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add differ-seam tests for `_effective_priority_map_for` and `_effective_create_defaults_for` mirroring test_effective_status_map_for_resolves_project + _honors_repo_root (resolve-project + repo_root-not-CWD).
evidence: outbound_differ.py `_effective_priority_map_for` / `_effective_create_defaults_for` docstrings: '``repo_root`` is the store root the pass runs against; ``[mapping]`` MUST be read from it, never the CWD.'

Contrast: test_status_mapping.py:324 test_effective_status_map_for_honors_repo_root exercises exactly this contract for the status axis (monkeypatch.chdir(decoy) then asserts the authoritative repo_root wins).
advisory.finding: The new differ seams `_effective_priority_map_for` and `_effective_create_defaults_for` (outbound_differ.py) have no test coverage, despite each carrying the stated `repo_root`-MUST-be-read-from-the-store-root-not-CWD contract. The parallel status seam has BOTH a resolve-project test and a repo_root-vs-CWD test (test_status_mapping.py:296, :324); the new priority/create_defaults seams have neither. A regression where these read the process CWD instead of the passed `repo_root` (silently resolving the wrong project's overlay) would not be caught.
scenarios: A reconcile pass run from a CWD that is not the store root: a CWD-relative read of `[mapping]` silently resolves the wrong project's priority_map / create_defaults.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two tests per new seam: one asserting a bound project's overlay is returned (and an empty mapping yields None), and one monkeypatching chdir to a decoy repo to prove `[mapping]` is read from the passed repo_root, not CWD.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test seeding a `priority_map`/`create_defaults` entry set to SKIP and assert the effective map omits that key.
evidence: config.py effective_priority_map: 'return {k: v for k, v in resolved.priority_map.items() if v != mc.SKIP}'
config.py effective_create_defaults: 'return {k: v for k, v in resolved.create_defaults.items() if v != mc.SKIP}'
effective_priority_map docstring: 'A ``SKIP`` value ... or an absent key means the local priority has NO Jira target — dropped here so callers see only mappable priorities'
advisory.finding: The `SKIP`-drop filter added to both `config.effective_priority_map` and `config.effective_create_defaults` (`{k: v for k, v in resolved.*.items() if v != mc.SKIP}`) is untested. No test seeds a `priority_map`/`create_defaults` entry whose value is SKIP to confirm that priority/default is dropped from the effective map (map-or-drift / field-omit). The tests only exercise overlay remap and injection, never the SKIP branch.
scenarios: An operator sets a priority_map or create_defaults entry to SKIP to explicitly drop a field; a regression that stops filtering SKIP would leak the literal SKIP sentinel into the effective map and thence the CREATE/UPDATE payload.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a project rebar.toml with e.g. `[mapping.projects.REB.priority_map]` `"2" = "skip"` and assert `"2" not in effective_priority_map('REB', root=proj)`; likewise for create_defaults.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the `inspect.signature(...).parameters` assertions with a behavioral check that a configured create_default never appears on an UPDATE payload.
evidence: test file:262-264: 'params = inspect.signature(OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote).parameters' / 'assert "priority_map" in params' / 'assert "create_defaults" not in params'
Litmus (Rule 4): a refactor renaming the update kwarg or bundling options while still never applying create_defaults on update would break these two asserts with no observable-behavior change.
advisory.finding: `test_create_defaults_not_applied_on_update` asserts on `inspect.signature(OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote).parameters` (`'create_defaults' not in params`). This half is a change-detector: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (renaming the kwarg, folding options into a dataclass/**kwargs) even though the observable contract — create-default fields never leaking onto an UPDATE payload — is unchanged. The signature introspection tests the function's internal shape, not its behavior.
scenarios: A future refactor reshapes the UPDATE mapper's parameter list without changing that create_defaults are never applied on update.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the two `params` asserts; instead configure a project with both a create_defaults entry and a priority_map, drive an UPDATE via the differ/update path, and assert the create-default field is absent from the update payload while the priority remap is present.
